record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For a closed immersed submanifold M of Euclidean space, define a generalized n-periodic billiard trajectory as an n-gon inscribed in M that is an extremal of perimeter. What lower bounds, in terms of the topology of M and of the immersion, can be proved for the number of such generalized periodic trajectories?

evidence.quote: estimate from below the number of generalized periodic trajectories

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a closed immersed smooth submanifold of Euclidean space. For an integer $n \geq 2$, define a generalized $n$-periodic billiard trajectory inscribed in $M$ to be an ordered $n$-tuple of points $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ on $M$ (an inscribed $n$-gon) that is a critical point of the perimeter functional
$$L(x_1, \dots, x_n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \|x_{i+1} - x_i\|, \qquad x_{n+1} := x_1,$$
where the variation is taken along the submanifold $M$ at each vertex. (Equivalently, at each vertex $x_i$ the difference of the unit vectors pointing to the neighboring vertices is normal to $M$ at $x_i$.)

Two such trajectories are identified if they differ by a cyclic permutation or reversal of their vertices.

Problem. Establish lower bounds, in terms of the topology of $M$ and of its immersion into $\mathbb{R}^N$ (e.g., dimension, codimension, homology, characteristic numbers), for the number of geometrically distinct generalized $n$-periodic billiard trajectories inscribed in $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: For the classical case where $M$ is a smooth closed convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^d$, lower bounds on the number of $n$-periodic (Euclidean and Finsler) billiard trajectories are known: for prime $n$ one has at least $(d-2)(n-1)+2$ geometrically distinct trajectories, with stronger estimates in general position. Extensions exist for outer/symplectic billiards on submanifolds. However, the general problem of lower bounds for arbitrary closed immersed submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Euclidean space remains open, with only partial results in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Counting Periodic Trajectories of Finsler Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: For prime r ≥ 3, the number of r-periodic Finsler billiard trajectories is not less than (r-1)(d-2)+1; stronger bounds in general position.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds known for the convex hypersurface (codimension-1) case.

status_evidence.title: Periodic Billiard Trajectories in Smooth Convex Bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bound (d-2)(p-1)+2 for prime p reflections per period in convex bodies in R^d.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp known lower bounds in the convex hypersurface case.

status_evidence.title: Outer symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: A submanifold of symplectic space determines a billiard-type correspondence; periodic orbits studied in higher codimension settings.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations to submanifolds of higher codimension are an active area.
